title: Requirement level (RFC 2119, as clarified by RFC 8174)
description: The requirement levels of a standard or specification: the BCP 14 key words, which carry their defined meaning only when written in capitals. Named by a `recommendation` block's `strength` in a folio whose issuing body writes requirements rather than graded recommendations (bean 55ao).

source.note: BCP 14: RFC 2119 and RFC 8174. The `technical-writer` voice in skills/voices/ applies the same levels.

codes.label: MUST
codes.definition: An absolute requirement of the specification; REQUIRED and SHALL mean the same.

codes.label: MUST NOT
codes.definition: An absolute prohibition of the specification; SHALL NOT means the same.

codes.label: SHOULD
codes.definition: There may be valid reasons in particular circumstances to ignore the item, but the full implications must be understood and weighed before doing so; RECOMMENDED means the same.

codes.label: SHOULD NOT
codes.definition: There may be valid reasons in particular circumstances when the behaviour is acceptable or useful, but the full implications should be understood before doing it; NOT RECOMMENDED means the same.

codes.label: MAY
codes.definition: The item is truly optional: an implementation may include it or omit it, and must interoperate with one that made the other choice; OPTIONAL means the same.
